skill.name: scikit-survival
skill.description: Comprehensive toolkit for survival analysis and time-to-event modeling in Python using scikit-survival. Use this skill when working with censored survival data, performing time-to-event analysis, fitting Cox models, Random Survival Forests, Gradient Boosting models, or Survival SVMs, evaluating survival predictions with concordance index or Brier score, handling competing risks, or implementing any survival analysis workflow with the scikit-survival library.
skill.summary: Build and evaluate survival models for censored time-to-event data with scikit-survival.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Censored time-to-event data requires specialized preparation, modeling, and evaluation. This skill guides practical scikit-survival workflows from outcome encoding through model comparison.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to represent censored outcomes with scikit-survival structures.
Guides selection among Cox, ensemble, and survival SVM models.
Provides preprocessing workflows for missing, categorical, and scaled features.
Compares concordance, time-dependent AUC, and Brier score metrics.
Covers Kaplan-Meier, Nelson-Aalen, and competing-risks estimation.
Shows cross-validation and hyperparameter-tuning patterns for survival models.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not execute analyses independently.
Users must supply valid datasets, dependencies, and domain-specific event definitions.
Clinical conclusions require expert review and external validation.
Some examples may require adaptation for installed scikit-survival versions.

use_cases.title: Analyze Clinical Follow-up Data
use_cases.description: Prepare censored outcomes, fit interpretable Cox models, and evaluate discrimination under censoring.

use_cases.title: Compare Survival Algorithms
use_cases.description: Benchmark Cox, forest, boosting, and SVM approaches with suitable survival metrics.

use_cases.title: Teach Time-to-Event Modeling
use_cases.description: Create structured examples covering preprocessing, model assumptions, validation, and competing risks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a First Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a scikit-survival model for my dataset. I have [rows], [features], [event rate], and [censoring rate]. Explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Survival Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a preprocessing workflow for [dataset description]. Include outcome encoding, missing values, categorical features, scaling, splitting, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Competing Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a fair comparison of [model list] using my training and test data. Select censoring-aware metrics and explain each metric.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Competing-Risks Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced competing-risks analysis for [event types]. Address cumulative incidence, cause-specific modeling, validation, assumptions, and interpretation limits.

output_examples.input: Which model should I use for 800 records, 25 features, moderate censoring, and interpretable effects?
output_examples.output: Start with a Cox proportional hazards model. Check proportional hazards, preprocess features consistently, and compare performance with a regularized Cox alternative.

output_examples.input: How should I evaluate predictions when 55 percent of observations are censored?
output: Use Uno's concordance index for ranking performance.
Add time-dependent AUC at clinically meaningful horizons.
Report integrated Brier score to assess calibration and discrimination.

output_examples.input: My study records relapse and death before relapse. How should I analyze relapse probability?
output_examples.output: Treat death before relapse as a competing event. Estimate cumulative incidence for relapse and avoid interpreting ordinary Kaplan-Meier estimates as event probability.

best_practices: Validate event indicators, time values, event counts, and censoring rates before fitting models.
Keep preprocessing inside cross-validation and apply training transformations unchanged to test data.
Report multiple censoring-aware metrics with assumptions, time horizons, and uncertainty.
anti_patterns: Do not treat competing events as ordinary censoring when estimating event-specific probabilities.
Do not select models using the test set or leak preprocessing across validation folds.
Do not use Harrell's concordance index alone when censoring is high.

faq.question: What data format does scikit-survival expect?
faq.answer: It commonly uses structured survival outcomes containing an event indicator and observed time, alongside a feature matrix.

faq.question: Which model is best for interpretable effects?
faq.answer: A Cox proportional hazards model is a common starting point when its assumptions are reasonable.

faq.question: When should I use a survival SVM?
faq.answer: Consider a survival SVM for medium-sized data where ranking performance matters and features can be scaled consistently.

faq.question: How should I handle high censoring?
faq.answer: Use censoring-aware metrics such as Uno's concordance index and verify that evaluation times are supported by the observed follow-up.

faq.question: Does this skill provide medical advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports statistical workflows, while clinical interpretation and decisions require qualified experts.

faq.question: Can this skill analyze competing risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains cumulative incidence and cause-specific approaches for mutually exclusive event types.
